cases.name: group-epics-from-software-requirements
cases.promptMarkdown: Group the software requirements in requirements/export/ into epics. I won't be around to answer questions, so do not wait for me.

graders.name: epics
graders.graderMarkdown:
The text is the `epics.md` the run wrote from a `software-requirements.md` with five software requirements for a report export: SWR-001 (accept up to 100 reports per request), SWR-002 (owner-only export), SWR-003 (nightly export), SWR-004 (audit record of every export) and SWR-005 (export of 10,000 rows within 30 seconds).

PASS if all of these hold:
- The grouping basis is stated first, before the epics (the user outcome by default).
- Each of SWR-001 to SWR-005 is on the `Covers:` line of exactly one epic, no software requirement is in two epics, and there is no list of requirements left out.
- Every epic has a goal, the `SWR-` IDs it covers, acceptance criteria that state observable behavior with at least one negative case (for example the 101st report rejected, or a teammate's request rejected), dependencies, risks and code areas.
- The acceptance criteria come from the verification criteria of the epic's software requirements, and an epic that holds the export-time requirement keeps 10,000 rows and 30 seconds in its criteria.
- A traceability table maps each `SYS-` to its `SWR-` and its `E-`.
- No epic states something that none of the five software requirements states.
FAIL if any of these is missing, if a software requirement is in no epic or in two, if the file is headed `Provisional`, or if an epic is invented.

graders.name: epics
graders.evidence:
# Epics — export

Grouping basis: the user outcome each epic delivers.

## E-01 — Export request rules

- Goal: a user can export up to 100 reports in one request, and only reports the user owns.
- Covers: SWR-001, SWR-002
- Acceptance criteria:
  - A request for 100 reports succeeds and returns 100 outputs.
  - A request for 101 reports is rejected with an error, and no output is written.
  - A request from the owner of a report succeeds.
  - A request from a teammate of the owner is rejected with an error, and no output is written.
- Depends on epics: none
- Risks: other limits in the service may still assume 50; the owner-only rule removes teammate access that users have today, so teammates need to be told.
- Code areas: `src/exporter.py:8`, `src/exporter.py:33`, `src/exporter.py:17-19`

## E-02 — Nightly export

- Goal: a user can schedule an export that runs every night, in UTC.
- Covers: SWR-003
- Acceptance criteria:
  - A scheduled export that is due runs once between 00:00 and 24:00 UTC, and its output is written.
  - A scheduled export that fails is reported to the user and runs again the next night.
- Depends on epics: E-01
- Risks: no scheduler exists, so one must be added; scheduled runs must obey the limit and owner rules from E-01.
- Code areas: new, beside `src/exporter.py`

## E-03 — Audit trail

- Goal: every export is recorded in the audit log.
- Covers: SWR-004
- Acceptance criteria:
  - After an export of 3 reports, the audit log holds 3 new entries, one per report.
  - An export that is rejected adds no entry for the report it rejected.
- Depends on epics: none
- Risks: the requirement is already met; the work is to verify it, and to keep it true when E-01 and E-02 change the export path.
- Code areas: `src/exporter.py:42`

## E-04 — Export speed

- Goal: a user gets a report of up to 10,000 rows exported within 30 seconds.
- Covers: SWR-005
- Acceptance criteria:
  - A report of 10,000 rows is exported in 30 seconds or less, measured from the request to the written output.
  - A report of 10,000 rows that takes 31 seconds fails the criterion.
- Depends on epics: none
- Risks: the time depends on the environment, so the measurement setup must be fixed before the criterion is trusted.
- Code areas: `src/exporter.py:22-27`

## Traceability

| System requirement | Software requirement | Epic |
| ------------------ | -------------------- | ---- |
| SYS-001 | SWR-001 | E-01 |
| SYS-003 | SWR-002 | E-01 |
| SYS-004 | SWR-003 | E-02 |
| SYS-006 | SWR-004 | E-03 |
| SYS-007 | SWR-005 | E-04 |

- Goal: every export is audited, and a report of up to 10,000 rows is exported within 30 seconds.
- Covers: SWR-004, SWR-005
- Acceptance criteria:

  - A report of 10,000 rows is exported in 30 seconds or less, measured from the request to the written output.
  - A report of 10,000 rows that takes 31 seconds fails the criterion.
- Depends on epics: E-01 (the rejection rules decide which exports are audited)
- Risks: SWR-004 is already met, so it is only verified here. - Code areas: `src/exporter.py:42`, `src/exporter.py:22-27`

# Epics — export

Grouping of the software requirements in `software-requirements.md`. Every SWR is in exactly one epic.

## EPIC-001 — Export governance

- Goal: Control who may export and how much, and keep a record of every export.
- Software requirements: SWR-001 (limit per request), SWR-002 (owner-only export), SWR-004 (audit record)
- System requirements: SYS-001, SYS-003, SYS-006
- Status: two change existing behavior (SWR-001, SWR-002); SWR-004 is already met

## EPIC-002 — Scheduled export

- Goal: Let a user have an export run on its own every night.
- Software requirements: SWR-003 (nightly export)
- System requirements: SYS-004
- Status: new; no scheduler exists

## EPIC-003 — Export performance

- Goal: Large reports export in a bounded time.
- Software requirements: SWR-005 (export time)
- System requirements: SYS-007
- Status: new

## Coverage

| SWR | Epic |
| --- | ---- |
| SWR-001 | EPIC-001 |
| SWR-002 | EPIC-001 |
| SWR-003 | EPIC-002 |
| SWR-004 | EPIC-001 |
| SWR-005 | EPIC-003 |

## Notes

- Grouping is by theme, chosen without asking the PO. SWR-004 could stand as its own compliance epic; it sits in EPIC-001 because it is a single, already-met requirement about the same export action.
